patch.summary:
Thesis: Same category, different company size — Both sit in business-communications, but documented company-size audiences diverge.

Frame: Same category, different company size — Both sit in business-communications, but documented company-size audiences diverge.. Choose Genesys only if your buying job matches “Enterprise CCaaS (Genesys Cloud CX) — CX 1 from $75/user/mo annual; CX 2 $115; CX 3 $155; ” rather than Ooma's shape. Choose Ooma only if your buying job matches “SMB VoIP (Ooma Office) — Essentials from $19.95/user/mo monthly; Pro $24.95; Pro Plus $29.” rather than Genesys's shape. Workflow advantage: Genesys leans contact-center, customer-messaging; Ooma leans business-phone. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Same category, different company size — Both sit in business-communications, but documented company-size audiences diverge.
- Positioning: Genesys is Enterprise CCaaS (Genesys Cloud CX) — CX 1 from $75/user/mo annual; CX 2 $115; CX 3 $155; CX 4 $240.; Ooma is SMB VoIP (Ooma Office) — Essentials from $19.95/user/mo monthly; Pro $24.95; Pro Plus $29.95 — no annual lock-in..
- Company-size focus: Genesys (mid-market, enterprise) vs Ooma (solo, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: Genesys-leaning contact-center, customer-messaging vs Ooma-leaning business-phone.
- Researched limits: Genesys — Enterprise complexity and implementation cost — not an SMB self-serve phone; Ooma — SMS allotments are account-wide caps (e.g. Pro ~250/mo) — not per-user unlimited.

Limitations — Genesys: Enterprise complexity and implementation cost — not an SMB self-serve phone; CX 1 is voice-only; digital channels require CX 2 or digital add-ons; Ooma: SMS allotments are account-wide caps (e.g. Pro ~250/mo) — not per-user unlimited; Call queues, CRM and auto-dialer require Pro Plus.

Poor-fit cases: Genesys is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Enterprise complexity and implementation cost — not an SMB self-serve phone · Ooma is a poor fit when that limitation bites: SMS allotments are account-wide caps (e.g. Pro ~250/mo) — not per-user unlimited · Avoid Genesys if you actually need Ooma's motion (SMB VoIP (Ooma Office) — Essentials from $19.95/user/mo monthly; Pro $24.95; Pro)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
